messages.subject: DSM error message
messages.body_plain:
Hello list,

I'm using Distance 6.0, Release 2, which I downloaded in January 2012. I'=
m trying to run a DSM analysis, single-observer data, and I am getting th=
e following error:

** Error: Encountered a problem while executing the data creating query '=
qry4_DsmObs.  **

Looking through the listserve, the help files and bugzilla, it seems this=
 is the bug that might be causing my problem:

Bug 85-=20
Single platform data error: =E2=80=9C** Error: Encountered a problem whil=
e executing the data creating query 'qry[x]_DsmSample. **=E2=80=9D=20

http://www.ruwpa.st-and.ac.uk/distance/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=3D85

I can see from the bugzilla site that this bug is resolved as of Septembe=
r 2010. Is there a patch for this problem? I've looked through the suppor=
t files without success.=20

Thank you very much for your help,
Natalie.

messages.subject: Re: DSM error message
messages.body_plain:
RESOLVED

Hello list,

Turns out my 'Error message' was caused by the Object column in my Observ=
ation data layer having been imported as 'Text' instead of 'Integer'. Onc=
e I re-imported the data and corrected this mistake, the analysis ran wit=
hout error.

To note: the MRDS and CDS analyses had run without errors which lead to m=
e assume I had correctly imported the data. But this was not the case.=20=

Many thanks to all that replied to my message.=20

Natalie.

--

> > Eric's right - it needs to be a multi-part polygon in the global layer.
> > Probably the easiest way to deal with the fragmented habitat situation is to
> > make a shapefile with one polgon for each habitat fragment, and then create
> > a stratum layer in distance with one record per fragment and then import the
> > shapefile into that layer. You then need to use a GIS to join the polygons
> > together and create a new shapefile layer with the multipart polygon. Then
> > import this new shapefile to the global layer. Now you're ready to create
> > the grid layer, and begin designing the survey. You could use the stratum
> > layer for the design and then you can do things like orient the lines
> > independently in each stratum. Hope this helps. Len

messages.subject_clean: Low encounter rate variance in point transect estimates
messages.body_plain:
I am attempting to estimate densities from point transect data.

In most results, Distance reports that Encounter rate contributes zero
to variance in the density estimate.

Here are some example point transect results:

              Point        Standard    Percent Coef.        95% Percent
  Parameter   Estimate       Error      of Variation     Confidence
Interval
  ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------
----------------------
    DS        1.2146      0.24249          19.97      0.81975
1.7996
    E(S)      1.6500      0.23255          14.09       1.2303
2.2129
    D         2.0041      0.48976          24.44       1.2419
3.2338
    N         160.00       39.102          24.44       99.000
259.00
  ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------
----------------------

 Component Percentages of Var(D)
 -------------------------------
 Detection probability   :  66.7
 Encounter rate          :   0.0
 Cluster size            :  33.3

Here are results for the same species from line transect data:

              Point        Standard    Percent Coef.        95% Percent
  Parameter   Estimate       Error      of Variation     Confidence
Interval
  ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------
----------------------
    DS        2.4688      0.46896          19.00       1.6884
3.6100
    E(S)      1.4286      0.17690          12.38       1.1045
1.8478
    D         3.5269      0.79972          22.68       2.2542
5.5181
    N         282.00       63.944          22.68       180.00
441.00
  ---------  -----------  -----------  --------------
----------------------

 Component Percentages of Var(D)
 -------------------------------
 Detection probability   :  34.6
 Encounter rate          :  35.6
 Cluster size            :  29.8

Why is encounter rate not contributing to variance in the point transect
estimate?

I am using Distance 6.0.

Stephen.

messages.subject: Point counts with 2 intervals
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

The UK Breeding Bird Survey delivers satisfactory estimates from line
transect data with two intervals (truncated at 100 m).

I am comparing some of my own line transect and point transect data,
both with two distance intervals.

Is it a bad idea to attempt to estimate the detection function from
point transect data with just two distance intervals? I am seeing
overestimation for some species compared to the line transect density
results.

I am using Distance 6.0 and assuming a half-normal model.

Are there any published studies where point transects with two distance
intervals have produced satisfactory estimates?

Stephen.

--

messages.subject: Intersecting transects and segments in DSM
messages.subject_clean: Intersecting transects and segments in DSM
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to use DSM for the first time, but struggling with how best to i=
mport the transects and segments.

I have two main blocks each with 26 north/south transects that are 25km lon=
g, which I'm happy enough dealing with.  However, I also have a 130km long =
transect that intersects many of the transects in the blocks.  The problem =
with this is that I end up with some segments that are included on 2 transe=
cts.

I have so far thought of 4 ways of dealing with this, but I'm not certain w=
hich is best.
1.  Allow segments to be included more than once, and listed separately on =
the respective transects.  My concern with this is that there will then be =
more than one density included in the analysis with habitat variables for a=
 specific segment which could be considered non-independent.
2. Combine the effort within the segments from all transects and remove the=
 transect layer (I'm not sure this is possible) and just have total line le=
ngth within a segment as the line length.
3. Retain the transect layer, but where segments overlap, attribute the all=
 of the segment effort (from both transects) to the block transect ID.
4. Only use the portions of the 130km transect that do not intersect the bl=
ocks (and reduce its total length).

Of course I could also remove the 130km transect, but that seems like a was=
te, and the transect also covers lots of areas that are not surveyed otherw=
ise.

Thanks,
Kate

The University of Aberdeen is a charity registered in Scotland, No SC013683=
.

messages.subject: Re: Intersecting transects and segments in DSM
messages.subject_clean: Intersecting transects and segments in DSM
messages.body_plain:
This is a good question Kate.

I won't suggest this is the 'correct' answer (other contributors to the
list may offer their opinions), but my suggestion would be to use your
option #1.  That respects the manner in which the data were collected.
I am not particularly bothered about the non-independence issue because
adjacent segments within a transect also have the non-independence
issue.  It is also the case that any point on the planet will not have a
static number of individuals and repeated visits will have a different
number of animals in the segment.  That is a rationale for dynamics
habitat covariates.
